title: dpw-2003-heavyweight
label: Mitch Armour

won.source: Pins Brian Reese in the final of the federation's first Heavyweight Championship tournament after a masked Malibu Mike Donovan costs Reese the match.

note: Lost the title to Mathias Mathews at Sex on the Beach after his own Prodigy stablemate Jason Kelly turned on him mid-match.

title: dpw-2003-heavyweight
label: Mathias Mathews

won.source: Pins Mitch Armour at Sex on the Beach after Jason Kelly, previously Armour's own Prodigy stablemate, attacks Armour behind the referee's back.

note: Still champion at the end of this record's own window (26 April 2004); the reign's later course is unread.

title: dpw-2003-tag-team
label: Kevin Spindler & Ken Sharper

won.source: Win a tag tournament final over Rufus Yoder and Brandon Storm at New Years Bash to become the federation's first Tag Team Champions.

note: The belts changed hands at least twice more before Intoxicated (a preview from 31 January 2004 already bills Thad Thorton and Brian Reese as champions, and one from 4 March 2004 bills Spindler with a new partner, Jason Kelly, instead of Sharper) but no card in this record shows either change; only the Mongs' own win over Spindler and Kelly at Intoxicated is directly attested.

title: dpw-2003-tag-team
label: The Mongs

won.source: Mong pins Kevin Spindler at Intoxicated after Mong 2 secretly swaps in for Mong mid-match.

note: Still champions at the end of this record's own window (23 April 2004), having retained the belts by disqualification at Beer Muscles and again at Under The Influence.

title: dpw-2003-intercontinental
label: Rufus Yoder

won.source: Wins the federation's first Royal Rumble, billed as also crowning the newly created Intercontinental Championship.

note: Still billed as champion as of 7 March 2004 (Burning Alcohol); by the next card in this record, 6 April 2004, Bill Fury is billed as champion instead, with no held document showing how the title changed hands — an untelevised pay-per-view called Spring Bash, mentioned but not itself posted to the newsgroup, is the presumed occasion.

title: dpw-2003-intercontinental
label: Bill Clinton

won.source: Slicer, until then Bill Fury's own opponent's rival, shoots Fury with a rifle from the crowd and rolls Clinton on top for the pin; Slicer joins Clinton's new stable afterward.

note: Still champion at the end of this record's own window (26 April 2004); an intervening reign by Bill Fury (won off-record, defended at Beer Muscles and Sex on the Beach, lost to Clinton) sits between this reign and Rufus Yoder's own, but Fury's own reign start is not attested by any held document and is not separately registered.

title: dpw-2003-heavyweight
label: "The Anti-Hero" Ice Kold

won.source: Knocks Mitch Armour out with concealed brass knuckles and pins him in the final of a second eight-man tournament, held after an eight-month gap in this record's own holdings.

note: Lost the title to Mitch Armour in a buried-alive match at Wacky Wiskey.

title: dpw-2003-heavyweight
label: Mitch Armour

won.source: Wins a buried-alive match after Eris Fury shoves both Ice Kold and his own valet into the grave.

note: A further card previewed but not held in this record, "Winner Drinks All," bills a Last Man Standing match between Mitch Armour and the Godfather for this title, and a still-later preview bills the Godfather as champion; no surviving document in the held record shows how the title actually changed hands.

title: dpw-2003-tag-team
label: Cable & Krypton

won.source: Cable and Krypton defeat Mr. Love and Corey "Outlaw" Davis for the vacant championship at Egg Nog Bash.

note: Lost the belts to JT Styles and Lil Blue at Wacky Wiskey.

title: dpw-2003-tag-team
label: JT Styles & Lil Blue

won.source: JT Styles pins Krypton with the Styles Clash at Wacky Wiskey.

note: Still champions at the end of this record's own window (8 February 2005).

title: dpw-2003-intercontinental
label: The Godfather

won.source: Wins the vacant championship by eliminating Big Daddy Magic last in a battle royal at Thirsty Turtle.

note: Surrendered the title outright to Rufus Yoder in exchange for a Heavyweight Championship shot, per the federation's own 20 January 2005 newsletter; no card in this record shows a match for the title changing hands, and Rufus Yoder's own reign is not separately registered for lack of one.

title: dpw-2003-womens
label: Buffy Summers

won.source: Pins Rachel Hilton to win the newly created championship at Wacky Wiskey.

note: Still champion at the end of this record's own window (8 February 2005); Eris Fury attacked her after the match and is billed against her in a barbwire steel cage match on a further card previewed but not held in this record.

title: dpw-1999-heavyweight
label: Extremeist

won.source: Won the title in the main event of the promotion's own Pack Keg Party card, with Bulldozer's assistance.

note: A follow-up news bulletin the same night frames this as the second half of a big fortnight, following a battle royal win at the promotion's previous pay-per-view.

title: dpw-1999-heavyweight
label: "Crazy Devil" Mitch Armour

won.source: Defeated the champion Extremeist while wrestling masked as "Masked Storm," with a co-conspirator's interference, then unmasked as the new champion.

lost.source: Lost the title to Badass John in a one-on-one main event, forced into the match alone after his own second was attacked backstage.

note: Retained once by disqualification against a challenger the week before losing the title outright.

title: dpw-1999-intercontinental
label: Madman

won.source: Already champion entering the earliest attestation in the held record (26 March 1999); no document in the held record records when or how he won it.

note: Retained in a falls-count-anywhere match against a challenger, with his own pet donkey kicking the challenger in the face for the assist.

title: dpw-1999-us
label: Polish Devil

won.source: Already champion entering the earliest attestation in the held record (26 March 1999); no document in the held record records when or how he won it.

note: Retained against a debuting challenger, whose face was burned by an exploding gift box a hooded interloper delivered mid-match.

title: dpw-1999-heavyweight
label: Badass John

won.source: The promotion's own broadcast script: defeated Mitch Armour by pinfall to reclaim the title he had lost weeks earlier.

note: The last surviving document reading on this title leaves Badass John champion; a further card and a following event are previewed but no results for either survive in the held record.

title: dpw-1999-heavyweight
label: Badass John

won.source: Already champion entering the earliest attestation in the held record (26 March 1999); no document in the held record records when or how he won it.

note: Lost the title in the main event when his own tag-team partner's rival, Bulldozer, pulled his legs out from under him mid-move.
